correctness.rationale: The exact order-eight criterion follows from full rational 2-torsion, two-primary rank two and the three nonzero torsion-halving conditions, including the necessary signs of -1. Positivity of the three differences makes the -1 quadratic character independent in a multiquadratic field. Chebotarev equidistributes the 2^(4-dimR) admissible sign quadruples; exhaustive enumeration of 16 F2^3 subspaces gives just 1/2,5/8,3/4,1. Each is explicitly realized by a verified rational cubic. A deterministic checker independently verifies 16 sign enumerations and 852 exact finite-field point counts; finite checks are not the infinite proof.

residual_risks: A more general existing theorem concerning Frobenius images on E[4] may imply the same density spectrum without spelling out all values.

Open-access abstracts of Gekeler 2006 and Achter-Wong 2013 were not sufficient to exclude every consequence of their full papers; both directly announced averaging over varying curves, not the fixed curve.
Unindexed or differently worded earlier classifications may exist; failure to find one is not a uniqueness proof.

value.rationale: The fixed-curve natural density of primes where the group has a point of order four is a canonical arithmetic invariant made natural by full rational 2-torsion. The theorem completes its possible-value classification, proves all values attained, and supplies a 3/4 density for the recently tabulated D(8) example, replacing finite empirical reduction data with an unconditional all-prime statement. This goes beyond restating the halving criterion: it requires and delivers the squareclass relation classification and global prime equidistribution. No higher-power or rate result claimed.
